situation: My coworker Jen presented our joint churn analysis to the VP yesterday and kept saying 'I found' for work I did. We're peers. I want to raise it with her one on one.
reply: Hey Jen, can I give you some feedback on yesterday's VP review? When you walked through the churn analysis, the cohort work I built came out as 'I found', and Marta left thinking it was all yours. I don't think you meant it that way. What's your read? For the next one, could we split the slides so each of us presents our own part?
note: Observation, impact, then pause for her side before the ask; there may be context you don't have.

situation: Just had a feedback conversation with my report Kevin about typos in client emails. Need the short written follow-up.
reply: Thanks for the chat this afternoon, Kevin. To capture it: client emails get a read-aloud check before sending, and for the next month anything to a new client comes to me for a quick look first. Let's check in on 13 November. Tell me if I've missed anything.
note: Neutral and short. The follow-up records the agreement, not the criticism.

situation: Three weeks ago I told my direct report Aisha she needs to stop showing up 20 minutes late to standup. It's still happening. I want to say it firmly in our 1:1.
reply: On 8 September we agreed you'd be at standup by 9:30, and you've been late four times since, including today. I need this to change now, and I'll be tracking it in our one-to-ones. What's getting in the way?
note: Name the agreement and the facts, make the consequence clear, and put it in writing after. If it continues, go to HR rather than repeating the conversation.

situation: 我是小组长，上周私下跟组员小周说过，他的周报数据连着两次算错，让他发之前自己核一遍。今天这份又错了，我提了一句，他回我：大家周报都有错，你怎么只盯着我。
reply: 我明白你觉得被单独挑出来了。其他人的周报有问题，我也会单独找他们谈，这里不拿你跟别人比。我们说的是你这边：最近三份周报都有数据算错，其中一处客户已经来问过。要求还是一样，另外加一步：接下来两周，周报周五下午四点前先发我过一遍再发出去。10月16号周五我们再聊聊效果。
note: 只有情绪、没有新信息的反驳：平静重复要求，给一个具体的支持措施和复盘日期，不展开辩论。

situation: My manager Greg keeps sending me 'urgent for Monday' tasks on Slack after 6pm on Fridays. Third week running, I worked Sunday again. I want to raise it in our 1:1 this Thursday without sounding like I'm complaining.
reply: Can I give you some feedback on how Friday requests reach me? The last three Fridays, urgent tasks have come in on Slack after 6pm for Monday morning, and I've ended up working Sundays to hit them. What's driving the timing on your side? If those could reach me by 3pm on Friday, or carry a Tuesday deadline when they land later, I can plan around them properly and still turn them round fast.
note: Upward feedback uses the same shape: ask first, the facts with a count, the impact, a real question, then an ask that makes his job easier too.

situation: 我是设计组长。同级的产品经理老吴上周四在需求评审会上当着大家说我组里新来的设计师小林的方案“完全没想过用户”，小林会后哭了。老吴人不坏，就是说话冲，我想私下跟他聊聊。
reply: 老吴，有空聊五分钟吗？想说说上周四评审会的事。你说小林的方案“完全没想过用户”，我知道你是着急方案有问题，但她刚来两个月，当着全组听到这句，这几天改稿都不太敢拿出来了。你当时主要觉得哪块有问题？以后评审遇到这种情况，能不能直接说具体是哪个环节，或者会后单独跟我说，我带她改。下周评审完我们再碰一下，看看效果。
note: 对平级同事：先征得同意，说具体一句话和它对团队的影响，先问他的看法，再提具体做法，并约好回头看。

situation: I manage a dev team. Marcus, a senior engineer, left three comments on junior dev Leah's pull request last Thursday that just said 'wrong, redo'. She told me she's now nervous about opening PRs. I'm raising it in our 1:1 tomorrow.
reply: Can I give you some feedback on code reviews? On Leah's pull request last Thursday, three of your comments said 'wrong, redo' with no explanation. She spent most of Friday guessing what you meant, and she's started sitting on PRs instead of opening them. What's your read on it? Going forward, I'd like every blocking comment to say what's wrong and point to one direction for the fix. Let's look at a couple of your reviews together on Tuesday 13 October.
note: A 1:1 script: pause after 'What's your read on it?' and actually listen before giving the ask; keep Leah's name out of it if he'd take it out on her.

situation: Yesterday I told my report Hannah that her weekly client reports keep arriving Monday afternoon instead of by 9am. She explained her kid's school start moved and she can't be online before 10 now. I didn't know. I want to follow up in writing with a revised ask.
reply: Thanks for telling me about the school run yesterday, that's useful context and I'm glad I know. What still matters is that clients have their reports when their week starts. So here's the adjusted ask: finish them by Friday 5pm and schedule them to send at 9am Monday, starting this week. If a Friday gets tight, tell me by Thursday and we'll move something off your plate. Let's check how it's going on Friday 16 October.
note: When pushback brings real context, change the ask, not the goal, and still put a check-in date on it.
